title: test-gates.json
description: The single source of truth for the test gates of one subproject (@t09tanaka/test-gates).

gates.description: Pure modules that hold an important decision. Each must reach 100% on all four coverage metrics and leave no surviving mutant outside its allow list.

candidates.description: Important logic that cannot be a gate yet. Nothing is enforced for these beyond their existence.

path.description: Path of the module, relative to the subproject, with forward slashes.

impact.description: What goes wrong for users or the business when the decision is wrong.

equivalentMutants.description: Surviving mutants that are allowed because they cannot be observed from outside. One entry allows exactly one mutant.

expectedTimeouts.description: Since 0.2.0. Mutants that can never finish (a loop that no longer ends) and therefore always time out. Same key as equivalentMutants. They are not counted against settings.mutation.maxTimeouts. An entry whose mutant survives, or does not exist, fails the run; one that is killed is accepted.

original.description: The source text the mutant replaces. Whitespace differences are ignored.

replacement.description: The text Stryker puts in its place. May be empty.

reason.description: Why no input can make the mutant observable.

occurrence.description: 1-based index among the mutants of the file with the same mutator, original and replacement. Required when there is more than one.

path.description: File or directory, relative to the subproject.

blocker.description: What has to happen before this can become a gate.

patternRule.description: A regular expression, either as a string or with flags and a reason.

defaults.description: Set to false to drop the built-in rules.

gateExtensions.description: File extensions a gate may have.

suffixes.description: Replaces the gate's extension to form the spec path. Default: ".spec<ext>" and ".test<ext>". An empty array means the project has no spec convention.

rewrite.description: Regular expression replacements applied to the gate path before the suffix, for specs that live in another directory.

impureImports.description: Modules a gate must not import at runtime (regular expressions tested against the module specifier). `import type` is never checked.

allow.description: Module specifiers exempt from every rule (regular expressions).

impureNamedImports.description: Names a gate must not import from a module that is otherwise fine. Default: PrismaClient from @prisma/client.

impurePaths.description: Gate paths that are rejected (regular expressions). Default: components and declaration files.

forbiddenSource.description: Lines that must not appear in a gate (regular expressions, tested one line at a time). Default: 'use client' / 'use server', and process.env (since 0.3.0).

importAliases.description: Import aliases, used to recognise a spec that mocks the module under test.

gateCommand.description: The command `test-gates selfcheck` runs. Default: `jest --config jest.gates.config.*` or `vitest run --config vitest.gates.config.*`, whichever config exists.

mode.description: Run the negative control for every gate, or only for the first.

failurePattern.description: Regular expression the output of the failing gate run must match. `{gate}` stands for the gate path. Default: a coverage threshold message on a line that names the gate.

reportFile.description: Where the Stryker JSON report is written and read.

file.description: Tracefile for `test-gates lcov` when --file is not given.

summaryExclude.description: Paths left out of the reference total (regular expressions).

imports.description: Since 0.2.0. How runtime imports of a gate are judged.

mode.description: blocklist (default): only the impureImports rules apply. allowlist: in addition, a runtime import must be relative, go through an import alias, or be listed in allow; a project import must not point at a file matched by impurePaths; a computed require() / import() is rejected.

allow.description: Packages a gate may import in allowlist mode. A string is a package name (its subpaths included). { pattern } is a regular expression tested against the specifier. { module, names } allows only those named imports.

maxTimeouts.description: How many timed-out mutants outside expectedTimeouts are tolerated. Above it the run fails. Default: 0 (since 0.3.0; before that, not set meant no limit).
